score.scope: Silent still-image story hierarchy, coherent atmosphere and visual rhythm/rest across the inspected whole frame and local scales. This is not an audio, animation, audience or deployed-banner score.

deductions.finding: 11 spreads irregular contour-like texture and bright flecks across materials that need different visual weights: hero face/antennae, bench planks, left bark, workshop box and open path. At full/native and 1280 this makes even the resting spaces busy and weakens the soft dimensional material hierarchy visible in07.

The workshop still communicates making mainly through the raised mallet and emphasis marks. The moth and Clawd face the viewer more than the task; Clawd therefore reads partly as a posed spectator rather than visibly attending to box-making. Dot provides the stronger inward attention cue.

The narrow 3:1 composition preserves coding at420, but the leaf-play relationship and workshop observer detail compress into small clusters. The three broad moth activities remain; the finer shared story cannot carry equal weight at that scale.

criteriaForNine: Recover clearly differentiated soft face/wing surfaces, wood grain and quiet path areas at native and1280 while retaining the warm light, same cast and current scene hierarchy; compare the actual result with07.
Strengthen workshop attention through a small pose/eyeline adjustment only if both Clawd square eyes and innocent moth anatomy remain clear; no extra effects, captions, sound or props.
Keep coding dominant at880/420 and accept secondary detail loss explicitly. A higher score does not require every guest interaction to remain readable at420.

strengths: One continuous tree/path/workshop/bench environment supports rest, making, play and coding without panel borders. The large coding moth remains the first read at all three supplied widths.
Scale, placement and the curved path separate the secondary groups from the bench. The four guests no longer form a single logo lineup and their localized activities do not usurp the hero.
Warm upper-right light, cooler distant pond/bridge and softer background forms provide coherent atmosphere and depth. Cloth canopy, blanket, books and steam give the scene lived-in warmth.
Muse and Grok share one leaf at the tree; resting moth closed eyes and folded mittens remain legible. The enlarged evidence shows dark Muse eyes and flat pupil-free white Grok ovals.
Silence is sufficient. No causal event requires sound to explain the depicted situation.

baselineComparison: 07 already has the same successful cast placement, three moth activities, warm light and open path.11 improves the visible Grok eye treatment and offers clear leaf contact in the enlarged tree evidence. However11 adds noticeably more wavy/segmented surface detail over hero fur, antennae, wood and ground;07 has calmer broader face and plank areas and cleaner workshop edges. This comparison supports selective repair, not a wholesale return that discards accepted eye corrections.
